name: Travary — Tavi paper suitcase v1
notes: Travary onboarding creative concept. Coral vintage carry-on, navy trim, brass corners, cream luggage tag, paper-fold arms, little wheels. Witty capable holiday porter. Canonical text-free opening frame; dimensional cut-paper/risograph travel-poster materials. Preserve front-panel face while rear-hinged lid opens.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: clean portrait 9:16 first-frame key art for an animated Travary onboarding scene. Full bleed scene, no UI, no text.
Reference image role: identity and art-direction reference only. Preserve the SAME original coral-orange paper suitcase character from the supplied hero: textured coral canvas, navy trim, brass corners, cream luggage tag, navy expressive eyes and brows, folded-paper arms, two little wheels. Keep the adult-friendly handmade paper-theatre and risograph travel-poster style. No redesign.
Primary request: Stage Tavi alone with its suitcase lid completely CLOSED on a beautiful simple physical paper set, ready to reveal an entire holiday world from inside. Three-quarter front view, whole character visible, located in the lower-middle of the portrait, occupying about 40 percent of image height. Witty self-assured half smile, one hand touching the top handle, other arm slightly extended in invitation. Cream luggage tag hangs naturally on the right side. Consistent asymmetric tactile paper textures and brass details.
Scene: deep petrol teal paper wall with visible subtle grain, pale warm cream paper floor, sophisticated warm stage light and a soft contact shadow. The upper half is clean teal negative space for a later pop-up landscape transformation. No foliage or destination visible yet, no other objects. Stable camera at suitcase eye level, spacious composition, character unclipped with room to gesture. Rich dimensional paper edges, stop-motion puppet craft, elegant travel brand colour.
Constraints: no letters, captions, wordmarks, screens, controls, maps, tickets, paper planes, people, confetti, extra limbs, glossy plastic, giant eyes or photorealistic materials. The closed-lid hinge and handle should be plausible and clear. This is a cinematic first frame, not a sheet of multiple poses.
